guardrail: Research is hypothesis generation only. No item in this file is allowed to change live predictions until separately validated.
research_summary: Evidence supports conditioning momentum versus reversal on turnover, liquidity, news intensity, intraday timing, and microstructure. The strongest research opportunities are event-defined continuation/exhaustion tests and leakage-safe discovery of recurring price-volume states.

hypotheses.title: Turnover-conditioned impulse continuation
hypotheses.claim: After a large intraday impulse, continuation is more likely when abnormal turnover and spread-adjusted dollar volume are high, especially with credible news, while low-turnover impulses reverse more often.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Separates information-driven demand from temporary liquidity pressure.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-, 15-, 30-, and 60-minute return; probability of making a new session high before a 2% drawdown.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher turnover and stronger news alignment should increase continuation; wider spreads without catalyst should increase reversal.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Chronological event study with cross-sectional bins, transaction-cost adjustment, and walk-forward thresholds.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Consistent monotonic relationship across at least three market eras and positive net expectancy after conservative spread and slippage assumptions.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No out-of-sample monotonicity, instability by price or float bucket, or disappearance after quote-based execution costs.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Bounce-count decay and failed reclaim severity
hypotheses.claim: Second and third bounces from the same support or VWAP area have lower magnitude and higher failure probability when each bounce forms a lower high, occurs on contracting volume, or fails to reclaim the prior impulse midpoint.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Directly tests exhaustion folklore using repeatable geometric and volume definitions.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability and time-to-failure for a 5% and 10% decline from the bounce high; maximum adverse excursion.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Later bounces should decay in size and fail faster, particularly after lower highs and volume contraction.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Define support algorithmically, avoid overlapping events, and run survival analysis plus out-of-sample quantile tests.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Stable increase in failure hazard across bounce counts with confidence intervals excluding zero and economically meaningful 5% drawdown separation.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Bounce-count effect vanishes under alternative support definitions or is explained entirely by volatility, spread, or time-of-day controls.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Climax-to-contraction exhaustion versus reacceleration
hypotheses.claim: A volume climax followed by declining volume, narrowing range, and repeated inability to hold above VWAP predicts exhaustion unless price accepts above the prior high with renewed relative volume.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Distinguishes a quick reflex bounce from genuine continuation after an impulsive move.
hypotheses.target_outcome: New-high continuation within 30 minutes versus failure below VWAP or impulse midpoint.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Contraction plus failed VWAP holds should predict failure; contraction followed by sustained volume expansion above the prior high should predict continuation.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Matched event study comparing identical impulse sizes, with competing-risk outcomes for new high and failure.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Improvement in out-of-sample ROC or precision-recall over impulse return alone, replicated across catalyst and non-catalyst samples.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Features add no incremental value after controlling for return, volatility, and relative volume, or depend on future-adjusted VWAP definitions.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity and time-of-day interaction
hypotheses.claim: Opening and closing-hour continuation differs from midday behavior: opening impulses are more continuation-prone when supported by informed volume, while late-day low-quality bounces have greater reversal and gap-risk exposure.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Intraday volume, spreads, liquidity demand, and return autocorrelation have strong time-of-day structure.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 15- and 60-minute return, close-to-close return, and probability of a 5% adverse move.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Opening informed impulses should continue more; late weak bounces should show higher failure hazard, especially with widening spreads and declining participation.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Minute-normalized features, separate open/midday/close samples, and purged walk-forward validation by date.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Time-of-day interaction remains significant after minute normalization and improves calibrated forward-risk estimates out of sample.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effect is eliminated by spread costs, varies unpredictably across venues, or fails during newer market-structure periods.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Step-plateau-reacceleration state
hypotheses.claim: A multi-session step-up followed by price acceptance in a narrow range can predict reacceleration when the plateau retains elevated turnover, higher lows, and stable or improving liquidity.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Tests whether accepted higher price levels differ from one-session spikes and failed breakouts.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Next-session or next-three-session probability of a fresh high, reacceleration return, and failure below plateau support.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher lows, retained turnover, and tight acceptance should increase reacceleration odds; falling turnover and failed breakout attempts should predict failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Session-level event study with purged dates, separate discovery and validation periods, and matched controls by prior return and volatility.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive forward-return spread and improved new-high classification in multiple unseen chronological validation blocks.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Pattern depends on arbitrary plateau length, loses value after controlling for momentum, or fails in a distinct historical regime.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Unsupervised price-volume motif discovery
hypotheses.claim: Leakage-safe clustering or shapelet discovery of normalized intraday price-volume-spread sequences can identify recurring states with materially different continuation, reversal, and failure-time distributions without starting from named setups.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: May uncover unknown motifs involving shape, volume timing, liquidity, or regime transitions that rule-based features miss.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Cluster-conditional forward return, new-high probability, 5%/10% drawdown hazard, and time-to-failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Some discovered motifs should show stable, economically distinct forward outcome distributions; most motifs should be rejected.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use an early training period for motif discovery, freeze transformations and cluster assignments, validate only on later unseen dates, and repeat with rolling walk-forward refits.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: A motif remains distinct across at least three later validation blocks, survives bootstrap and multiple-testing controls, and improves calibrated prediction over simple baselines.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Performance requires same-period discovery, collapses under symbol/date holdouts, is driven by a few names, or fails after spread and slippage costs.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

important_caveats: Small-cap and low-priced stocks have severe selection, halt, borrow, quote, and survivorship biases.
Use point-in-time float, shares outstanding, corporate actions, news timestamps, and delisting data.
Define all indicators using only information available at the event timestamp; avoid full-day VWAP, future session highs, and revised fundamentals.
Use purged and embargoed validation when events overlap or labels span multiple bars or sessions.
Report precision-recall, calibration, hazard curves, turnover, maximum adverse excursion, and cost-adjusted outcomes rather than returns alone.
research_gaps: Reliable public intraday datasets combining trades, quotes, halts, venue information, borrow constraints, and point-in-time float remain limited.
The severity and timing of second- and third-bounce failures in catalyst-driven low-float stocks need larger cross-sectional samples.
More evidence is needed on whether anchored VWAP acceptance adds information beyond price, volume, and range features.
Discovery methods should be compared on stability, interpretability, multiple-testing control, and robustness to changing tick sizes and venue structure.
